newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish Riksbank sets repo at unchanged 4.35 pct.
newsitem.headline: Swedish Riksbank sets repo at unchanged 4.35 pct.

text.p: Sweden's central bank, the Riksbank, on Tuesday set its weekly reverse repurchase operation at a fixed, unchanged 4.35 percent, as expected.
The operation will run from December 11 to December 18.
The repo rate, is the bank's key tool for controlling money market liquidity and the central in a three tier system.

Eight out of 10 analysts polled by Reuters did not expect the Riksbank to lower its key rate but forecast another cut next week on December 17 when the central bank is due to release its latest inflation report.
The Riksbank has already said that the repo set on December 17 will run for three weeks to cover the holiday period.
"There is room for a cut but the Riksbank will probably wait until the inflation report is released on December 17," one economist told Reuters.
Forecasts for the December 17 cut varied from five basis points to 25, but most forecasts ranged between 10 to 20 points.

The economists surveyed said the repo rate was close to bottoming. Several said it would hit bottom in January while others said it would happen in the first quarter when it reached between 3.75 and four percent.
The average for the bottom repo rate was 3.90 percent.
The interest rate corridor's floor, or deposit rate, is 3.75 percent and its ceiling, or lending rate is 5.25 percent following a widely-expected 50 basis point cut last Thursday.
